text:
Recent work supports separating temporal intent and multiple interests. [MSMT-LSI (2024)](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44196-024-00460-5) uses separate attention networks for long- and short-term preferences, multiple temporal embeddings, and hybrid fusion. [HM4SR (WWW 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.14269) combines an interest-filtering MoE with a temporal MoE using explicit timestamp embeddings; auxiliary contrastive tasks address sparsity. Its category-prediction supervision requires metadata unavailable in this benchmark. [MGUI (2026)](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/11506283) combines interval-aware gates for individual recent interactions, capsule-guided attention for groups of recent interactions, and global item-transition propagation, with user-specific expert weighting.

For multiple preference representations, [PoMRec (2025)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40266875/) distinguishes interest extraction from aggregation and models both the mean and variance of interaction embeddings. These papers motivate a benchmark-compatible hypothesis: augment SASRec with a recent-history branch and several attention-pooled persistent-interest vectors; learn their fusion from observed history length, timestamp gaps, and sequence features. Use only historical timestamps at prediction time, since the next interaction time is unknown. For sparse purchase histories, begin with few experts and modest capacity; inspect routing collapse and gate behavior by history length. These are proposed adaptations, not established gains on the four-category benchmark. Validate their contribution through temporal-gate and multi-interest ablations using macro validation HR@10; neither purchases nor timestamps establish satisfaction, ownership, or latent user traits.
